extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of classical literature / literary criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and evaluative principles for judging ancient Greek poets, their myths, and related imitative arts (drama, sculpture), with attention to historical context, moral effects, language, and allegory. Emphasizes how to balance collective cultural defects against individual artistic merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish collective defects from individual merit
rubrics_metrics.description: When a common defect of antiquity is once distinctly recognized as one, the reproach of which affects ... the collective character, manners, and literature of antiquity, it were absurd ... to refuse ... to perceive in Aristophanes the great poet which he really is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not allow general cultural imperfections to obscure the individual poet's great qualities; evaluate writers on their personal merits even if they share broader period faults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for historical/contextual licence (festival/democracy)
rubrics_metrics.description: All the peculiarities of the 'old comedy' may be traced to those deifications of physical powers ... in the festivals dedicated to Bacchus ... every sort of freedom ... were not only things permitted, they were strictly in character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess formal peculiarities (wildness, audacity) in light of the social and ritual contexts that permitted them (e.g., Saturnalian licence, democratic licence in Athens) rather than condemning them out of modern context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain poetical dignity despite extravagance
rubrics_metrics.description: The true poet ... was uniformly impressed ... by the highest elegance of language and versification, to maintain entire his poetical dignity ... and to show in the midst of all his extravagances, that he was not animated by prosaic petulance, nor personal spleen, but inspired with the genuine audacity and fearlessness of a poet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge comic or licentious poems by whether their extravagances are rooted in poetic imagination and dignity rather than petty spite or mere prosaic malice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence of language and versification
rubrics_metrics.description: In language and versification his excellence is not barely acknowledged — it is such as to entitle him to take his place among the first poets to whom Greece has given birth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate technical craft — choice of language, rhetorical figures, and versification — as primary indicators of poetic greatness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of serious/earnest poetry within popular forms
rubrics_metrics.description: In many passages of serious and earnest poetry which ... he has here and there introduced, Aristophanes shows himself to be a true poet, and capable, had he so chosen, of reaching the highest eminence even in the more dignified departments of his art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and weigh instances where a poet within a popular or comic form achieves moments of elevated, serious poetry; such passages indicate broader capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obscenity and filth as disfiguring defects
rubrics_metrics.description: However much his writings are disfigured by a perpetual admixture of obscenity and filth ... after deducting from the computation everything that is either offensive or obscure, there will still remain ... wit, fancy, invention, and poetical boldness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify obscene or filthy elements and consider deducting their effect when assessing overall merit, while still acknowledging surviving intellectual and imaginative riches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess surviving wit/fancy after removing offensive/obscure elements
rubrics_metrics.description: After deducting ... everything that is either offensive or obscure, there will still remain ... a luxurious intellectual banquet of wit, fancy, invention, and poetical boldness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform a 'net' evaluation: separate and subtract purely offensive/obscure matter to reveal the work's core inventive and poetic qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political courage and fidelity in satire
rubrics_metrics.description: His principal merit as a patriot consists in the fidelity with which he paints all the corruptions of the state, and in the chastisement which he inflicts on the pestilent demagogues who caused that corruption or profited by its effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value a poet's civic function: faithful, fearless exposure of political corruption and willingness to risk reprisal are marks of merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider danger and resolution in political critique
rubrics_metrics.description: The latter duty was attended with no inconsiderable danger in a state governed by a democracy, and during a time of total anarchy — yet Aristophanes has performed it with the most fearless resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When appraising satire, account for the risks the author took and the resolve shown in addressing dangerous public issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness of satirical tone toward peers
rubrics_metrics.description: He pursues and parodies Euripides with unrelenting severity; but ... not only the more ancient Aeschylus, but even his cotemporary Sophocles, is uniformly mentioned in a tone altogether different, in a temper moderate and sparing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether satire is targeted with proportionate severity and whether the poet shows discernment and moderation in his critical tone toward different peers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret authorial intent in use of famous names
rubrics_metrics.description: It is by no means improbable that this (the odious representation of Socrates) was not the effect of mere poetical wantonness; but that Aristophanes selected ... that he might under it render the Sophists as ridiculous as they deserved to be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid assuming malice: consider whether the poet used a famous figure as a rhetorical vehicle to attack a class or idea rather than the individual per se.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poet's civic/intellectual aim: refuting sophistry and restoring truth
rubrics_metrics.description: The utter vanity of whose doctrines induced him to begin the arduous attempt to revolutionize the whole intellectual character of his countrymen, and reinstate truth in her rightful supremacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the poet's attacks serve a higher intellectual purpose (e.g., exposing sophistry, promoting truth) rather than mere ridicule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate philosophical/spiritual depth vs materialism in myth
rubrics_metrics.description: Those principles ... concerning God and man — were far too material, and, in effect, if not despicable, at least unsatisfactory ... In this theology there is contained, in fact, absolute materialism ... clothed in poetical form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging mythopoetic works, consider whether their theology/philosophy rises above crude materialism to offer spiritual or intellectual depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mythological symbolism can be hostile to aesthetic beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: All these symbolical images are hostile to the beauty of imitative representations ... The representation of a hundred-handed giant ... in a work of sculpture ... we should be as much shocked with the deformity of this Grecian image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate symbolic/mythic motifs for their compatibility with aesthetic form, especially in visual arts; literal symbolic embodiments may produce deformity rather than beauty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imitative arts (sculpture) should avoid literal grotesque symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: The art of sculpture reached accordingly far greater perfection among the Greeks than it ever attained among the Egyptians, merely because the former people did not adhere so pertinaciously as the latter to those ancient symbols, but were perpetually laying them more and more aside, in so far as they were chargeable with deformity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For sculptural/visual representation, prefer humanized or refined forms of divinity over literal, grotesque symbolisms if beauty of form is a goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poets should soften and polish barbarous mythic elements
rubrics_metrics.description: It was uniformly attempted by all their serious poets ... to soften down and polish away those rough and barbarous circumstances in their ancient mythology, which are most offensive to a refined understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value the poet's refining work: transforming crude mythic materials into expressions palatable to refined taste is a mark of poetic craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer allegorical/interpretive readings of mythic passages
rubrics_metrics.description: At first sight this appears to be nothing more than a piece of rough and swaggering redomontado, yet there is no doubt that in this passage reference is made to the chain-like connection which runs through all things ... So accordingly was this allegory universally explained among the ancients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor allegorical or hieroglyphical interpretations over merely literal readings to recover original meanings and to avoid misjudging passages as crude or absurd.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider ethical influence of poetic fictions on popular morals
rubrics_metrics.description: How could the ancient moralists consider so lightly poetical fictions which formed the root and essence of the popular creed of their country? ... the pernicious influence on the character of those who adopted it, was every day before their eyes, in the willing zeal with which their believing countrymen imitated the moral transgressions of their gods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating works intended for popular belief, weigh their moral effects: poets whose fictions encourage immoral imitation may be judged harshly on ethical grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate individual poets from general mythology
rubrics_metrics.description: Before we can judge aright of this matter, we must draw a line of distinction between Homer, individually considered, and the ancient mythology taken as a general system of belief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate an individual poet's contributions and influence from the broader, often defective, mythological system when forming critical judgments.
